rounds.proof_sketch: K=512, TILE_SIZE=32, so K is perfectly divisible. Loop runs t∈[0,15], last tile has tiled_k=480. Max index = 480+31=511. Condition (511 < 512) ≡ (511 <= 512) ≡ true. The case (index==512) where < and <= differ is never reached.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes behavior only when tiled_k + threadIdx.x equals exactly K. With K=512 and TILE_SIZE=32, the input dimension K is perfectly divisible by the tile size. This means the loop processes exactly 16 complete tiles, with the maximum accessed index being 511 (from tiled_k=480, threadIdx.x=31). Since 511 < 512 and 511 <= 512 are both true, and no iteration ever produces tiled_k + threadIdx.x = 512, the boundary case where the relational operator change matters is structurally unreachable.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed K=512 configuration. The mutation would only be killable if K were not a multiple of TILE_SIZE (e.g., K=500), which would create a partial last tile where the boundary case could be reached.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for tiled GPU kernels should include configurations where dimensions are NOT exact multiples of tile sizes, as these boundary cases are where off-by-one errors in bounds checks become observable.
